nodes.idea: Preprints with shorter titles collect more citations at two years because search engines retrieve them more often. If so, shortening titles is a cheap lever for visibility.
Keep the goal (raise retrieval visibility) and change the mechanism: the coverage of query terms in the abstract, not the length of the title, is the lever.
nodes.title: Abstract term coverage instead of title length

nodes.idea: Transfer the headline-length findings of news search to preprint titles in scholarly search.
nodes.title: News headline length applied to preprint titles

nodes.idea: Use the literature on query-title matching in dataset retrieval as an intermediate concept that links the idea to a neighbouring field.
nodes.title: Title-term matching in dataset search as a bridge

nodes.idea: Explain the association that survives the journal adjustment by author-level skill in crafting titles.
nodes.title: Author title-crafting skill as the residual

nodes.idea: Invert the hypothesis: in narrow fields, longer and more specific titles are retrieved more because they match precise queries.
nodes.title: Longer titles gain in narrow fields

nodes.idea: Since the retrieval effect held on preprints, extend its scope to journal records of the same fields.
nodes.title: Same retrieval test on non-preprint records

nodes.idea: Transfer the confirmed retrieval lever to the titles of datasets in open data repositories.
nodes.title: Transfer to dataset titles in data repositories
